title: Design System: Taskscape
note: Taskscape is a native macOS app (Rust + Iced), not a web project. The live preview panel renders HTML/CSS in a browser and does not apply here, so component HTML/CSS snippets are intentionally omitted. This sidecar carries the framework-agnostic extension data (color metadata, tonal ramps, shadow vocabulary, narrative) that augments DESIGN.md. Values reflect the canonical DARK theme; light-theme counterparts are documented in DESIGN.md §2.

display.purpose: The editable list title only — the one large, confident moment (Poppins SemiBold 40px).

headline.purpose: Primary screen/section headings and empty-state titles (Poppins SemiBold 26px).

title.purpose: Modal titles and sub-section headers (Poppins SemiBold 17–22px).

body.purpose: Task text, button labels, input values (Inter Regular 14–16px).

label.purpose: Captions, chips, metric counts, quiet metadata (Inter Regular 11–13px).

shadows.name: action-lift
shadows.purpose: The primary (coral) button only — a soft halo that says 'press me'; removed on :active.

shadows.name: modal-lift
shadows.purpose: The centered modal card floating above its dimmed backdrop.

shadows.name: sidebar-edge
shadows.purpose: Cast rightward onto the content area so the sidebar reads as a raised plane, not a seam.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Coral fill with Accent-Ink text and the action-lift shadow; the single primary action per view. Hover lightens ~8% toward white; press drops the shadow.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Translucent raised panel (35%) with a 1px resting border; the quiet secondary action. Hover warms the border to border-strong.

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: Solid panel-raised fill, 1px border, 12px radius; optional count beside the glyph.

components.name: Plain Icon Button
components.description: Transparent, borderless, faint hover tint only; for actions nested inside an already-styled row (e.g. per-task paperclip).

components.name: Input Field
components.description: panel-raised background, 12px radius, 1px border; focus shifts the border to full Ember Coral, selection at 28% accent.

components.name: Dropdown (pick list)
components.description: Matches the input; hover/open warm the border to border-strong, handle glyph in text-secondary.

components.name: Accent Chip
components.description: panel-alt fill, 16px radius, Accent-Ink label; for attachment chips and small badges.

components.name: Modal Card
components.description: panel-alt surface, 16px radius, border-strong edge, modal-lift shadow above a dimmed backdrop.

components.name: Mini Window
components.description: Signature hotkey-summoned capture popup: transparent window clipped to 10px radius with a 1.5px Ember-Coral hairline border at 45% alpha; no drop shadow (native CALayer clip).

components.name: Editable Title
components.description: Signature 40px Poppins SemiBold list title that flips in place between display text and a borderless inline field; the capture-first way to rename a list.

narrative.overview: Taskscape is an uncluttered, deliberately arranged personal desk. Nothing extra sits on it; everything that is there is there on purpose and within easy reach. The surface is warm — terracotta, amber, toasted browns — so it feels lived-in and calm rather than clinical, but the warmth never tips into decoration. A single coral accent is the one tool you reach for most, and its rarity is what makes it read as 'the action.' Depth comes from tonal layering (bg → panel-alt → panel-raised), not from heavy shadows; shadows are rationed for surfaces that genuinely lift. The system rejects the corporate SaaS dashboard, sterile gray minimalism, visual clutter, and gamification. Calm confidence is the register; the design earns its keep by getting out of the way.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, tonal, low-contrast surfaces; warmth carried by palette and type, never decoration.
One coral accent, used sparingly, as the single 'this is the action' signal.
Tonal layering over shadows; depth is rationed and meaningful.
Soft, friendly radii (10–16px); the square sidebar is the deliberate exception.
Full dark/light parity — both themes first-class, both legible (WCAG AA).

rules.name: The One Ember Rule
rules.body: Ember Coral appears on a single primary affordance per view. If two things on screen are coral, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Dual-Theme Parity Rule
rules.body: Every color exists in both themes and both must ship at full quality. A change to a token is a change to both of its values.

rules.name: The Warm-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows and borders are tinted toward the surface's own warm hue, never neutral gray or pure black.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Poppins speaks for structure (titles, headings); Inter speaks for content and controls.

rules.name: The Quiet-Type Rule
rules.body: Size and weight carry hierarchy; tracking and case do not. No all-caps tracked eyebrows.

rules.name: The Earned-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface gets a shadow only if it physically lifts: the primary action, a modal, the sidebar edge. Everything else separates by tone.

dos: Do reserve Ember Coral for one primary action per view; build other hierarchy from the neutral ladder and type weight.
Do convey depth with tonal layering before reaching for a shadow.
Do keep both themes at full quality and verify contrast in each (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large).
Do route every style through common::thememanager factories and build UI from the t_* toolkit.
Do tint borders and shadows toward the surface's warm hue.
Do keep capture frictionless: hotkey → type → Enter and the mini window stay ceremony-free.
Do honor the system reduced-motion preference with a crossfade or instant fallback.
donts: Don't build toward a corporate SaaS dashboard — no dense data-grid chrome, no enterprise blue.
Don't drift into sterile gray minimalism — no cold flat gray/white surfaces, no neutral-black shadows.
Don't clutter the surface — every control earns its place or is removed.
Don't gamify — no confetti, streaks, mascots, badges, or bright primary colors.
Don't let text-muted sit on a low-contrast surface for anything that must be read, placeholders included.
Don't add a second coral element, a decorative gradient wash, or a shadow 'to make it pop.'
Don't use all-caps tracked eyebrows or letter-spacing tricks for hierarchy.
